findings.title: Null item lists now cause an unhandled NullPointerException in subtotal
findings.evidence: The method iterates directly over the caller-provided list without any null check, so a reachable call like subtotal(null) will throw before any billing error can be reported cleanly.
findings.recommendation: Validate 'items' at method entry and throw a clear IllegalArgumentException, or treat null as an empty list if that matches the API contract. Also consider validating that no element in the list is null before dereferencing it.

findings.title: totalWithTax accepts null or negative tax rates and can crash or return invalid negative totals
findings.evidence: Tax is computed from the raw caller input with no validation, so totalWithTax(items, null) will throw a NullPointerException and negative rates less than -1 can drive the invoice total below zero.
findings.recommendation: Reject null tax rates explicitly and enforce an allowed range such as 0 to 1, or whatever the business contract requires. If credits or discounts are intended, model them separately instead of overloading taxRate.
